WHAT THIS PROGRAM REPLACED WAS MEASURED SILENT, twice, before a line of it
was written. The reading lived in `.githooks/pre-push` as three `gh -q`
expressions, and the suite that holds that hook up stubs `gh` with lines it
has already filtered. Renaming `.conclusion` to `.verdict` there left the
hook suite at 14 passed / 0 failed while a real `gh` prints every conclusion
as `-`, so a RED commit reports clean; renaming `annotations_count` to
`annotation_count` left it at 14 passed / 0 failed while every commit reports
no annotations at all. Both are silent in the direction that reads as good
news. That is the class this crate exists to make loud, and every injection
below removes one distinction it draws and names the test that must go red.
Scoped to this crate's own suite: nothing here touches the tree it reports
on, so running the repository's whole suite would be minutes of proving
nothing. The hook's half — that it CALLS this reporter and carries its words
